## Winter Chapter 1

this is code from chapter 1 of the winter textbook.

```{r}
numbers <- c(18, 1024, 92, 73, 14)
sum(numbers)
mean(numbers)
sd(numbers) %>% round(digits = 2) # can include 'digits =' but don't need to because r recognizes the order of arguments; round(digits = 2) is the same as round(2)
sd(numbers) %>% round(2)

names <- c("dana", "charlie", "louis", "ari") # store these names as a list; reminder c() stands for concatenate

# read in the data
data_nettle <- read_csv("nettle_1999_climate.csv") # note, winter uses capitalization

# inspect the data
str(data_nettle) # base R inspect the dataframe
glimpse(data_nettle) # tidyverse inspect the dataframe

# make a plot of population by area
# note 
ggplot(data = data_nettle, aes(x = Population, y = Area)) +
  geom_point(
    color = "blue",
    shape = 21,
    size = 3
  )
# make a histogram of values
ggplot(data_nettle, aes(Population)) +
  geom_histogram()
```

##  Winter Chapter 2

### 2.11.3

```{r}
data_nettle <- read_csv(here("Data", "nettle_1999_climate.csv"))
# show data only for Benin
data_nettle %>%
  filter(Country == "Benin")
# show data from Benin and Zaire
data_nettle %>%
  filter(Country %in% c("Benin", "Zaire"))
# show only Langs column
data_nettle %>%
  select(Langs)
# show Langs data for Benin
data_nettle %>%
  filter(Country == "Benin") %>%
  select(Langs)
# show data for Population to MGS columns for Benin
data_nettle %>%
  filter(Country == "Benin") %>%
  select(Population:MGS)
# return rows where Langs > 200
data_nettle %>%
  filter(Langs > 200)
# return rows where Langs > 200 and Population < median(Population)
data_nettle %>%
  filter(Langs > 200,
         Population < median(Population))
```

### 2.11.4

```{r}
data_nettle %>%
  filter(Population < 4) %>%
  mutate(
   MGS_cat = ifelse(MGS < 6, "dry", "fertile") 
  ) %>%
  group_by(MGS_cat) %>%
  summarize(LangSum = sum(Langs))

# using case_when
data_nettle %>%
  filter(Population < 4) %>%
  mutate(
    MGS_cat = case_when(
      MGS <  6 ~ "dry",
      MGS >= 6 ~ "fertile",
      .unmatched = "error"
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(MGS_cat) %>%
  summarize(LangSum = sum(Langs))

# example
data_nettle %>%
  filter(Population < 4) %>%
  mutate(
    MGS_cat = case_when(
      MGS <  4 ~ "very dry",
      MGS <  6 ~ "dry",
      MGS <  8 ~ "fertile",
      MGS >= 8 ~ "very fertile",
      .unmatched = "error"
    ),
    MGS_cat = fct_relevel(MGS_cat, "very dry", "dry", "fertile", "very fertile")
  ) %>%
  group_by(MGS_cat) %>%
  summarize(LangSum = sum(Langs))

# sanity check: does case_when operate the way i think it does
data_nettle %>%
  mutate(
    MGS_cat = case_when(
      MGS <  4 ~ "very dry",
      MGS <  6 ~ "dry",
      MGS <  8 ~ "fertile",
      MGS >= 8 ~ "very fertile",
      .unmatched = "error")
    ) %>%
  group_by(MGS_cat) %>%
  count()

# get descriptive statistics for the smallpopulation data
data_nettle %>%
  filter(Population < 4) %>%
  mutate(
    MGS_cat = case_when(
      MGS <  4 ~ "very dry",
      MGS <  6 ~ "dry",
      MGS <  8 ~ "fertile",
      MGS >= 8 ~ "very fertile",
      .unmatched = "error"
    ),
    MGS_cat = fct_relevel(MGS_cat, "very dry", "dry", "fertile", "very fertile")
  ) %>%
  group_by(MGS_cat) %>%
  summarize(mean = mean(Langs) %>% round(2),
            sd = sd(Langs) %>% round(2),
            min = min(Langs),
            max = max(Langs))
```

## Winter Chapter 3

```{r}
# generate and plot a normal distribution
rnorm(50) %>%
  hist() # base r

# set the mean and sd
rnorm(50, 71.82, 10.42) %>%
  hist() 

# with ggplot
rnorm(50, 71.82, 10.42) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename(score = 1) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = score)) +
  geom_histogram(color = "black", fill = "white")

# with 12 participants
rnorm(12, 71.82, 10.42) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename(score = 1) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = score)) +
  geom_histogram(color = "black", fill = "white")
# with 1200
rnorm(1200, 71.82, 10.42) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename(score = 1) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = score)) +
  geom_histogram(color = "black", fill = "white")

# how would we screen / filter scores > 100 and < 0


```

### Emotional valence

```{r}
# read the data
data_war <- read_csv(here("Data", "warriner_2013_emotional_valence.csv"))

# look at the variables
glimpse(data_war)

# take the range using base r
range(data_war$Val)

# look up the word with the minimum and maximum valence (return the row matching those conditions)
data_war %>%
  filter(Val == min(Val) | Val == max(Val))

# what else could we do with the data
```

### 3.10.1

```{r}
data_war %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Val)) +
  geom_histogram(color = "black", fill = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(data_war$Val), size = 2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(data_war$Val) - sd(data_war$Val), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(data_war$Val) + sd(data_war$Val), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(data_war$Val) - 2*sd(data_war$Val), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(data_war$Val) + 2*sd(data_war$Val), linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_minimal()
```

### 3.10.2

```{r}
data_war %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Val)) +
  geom_density(color = "black", fill = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(data_war$Val), size = 2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(data_war$Val) - sd(data_war$Val), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(data_war$Val) + sd(data_war$Val), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(data_war$Val) - 2*sd(data_war$Val), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(data_war$Val) + 2*sd(data_war$Val), linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_minimal()
```
